questions.question_text:
In Dijkstra's algorithm starting at vertex $S$, vertex $C$ has a direct edge $SC = 10$, but its recorded label is $8$.
Which statement best explains why?

options.text: An indirect path from $S$ to $C$ via another vertex has a total weight of $8$, which is shorter than the direct edge
The algorithm subtracted $2$ because vertex $C$ is two edges away from the start
options.why: Dijkstra's algorithm never subtracts distance for edge counts.

options.text: The weight of the direct edge was discounted because $C$ has an even degree
options.why: Vertex degrees do not discount or alter edge weights in Dijkstra's algorithm.

options.text: The direct edge $SC$ was excluded because it forms a cycle in the graph
options.why: Dijkstra's algorithm operates on general graphs and does not drop edges due to cycles.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Label}(C) = \min(10, 8)$
$= 8$
An indirect path from $S$ to $C$ has a lower cumulative weight of $8$ than the direct edge weight of $10$.
